Connector history bridge callers reach this operation; allowed-directory defaults include the process temporary-directory category.
findings.trigger: A local or agent-controlled writer can replace a permitted file or directory between authorization/stat and pathname read, or grow the permitted file after stat. Requires write control of the allowed path; no unauthenticated remote path access is claimed.
findings.impact: The bridge can publish process-readable bytes from outside the allowlist and exceed its configured read limit; readFile may allocate a large buffer before the later upload cap rejects it.
findings.recommendation: Authorize and open a pinned descriptor with no-follow protections, verify file identity/type against the authorized stat and account for parent-directory replacement. Read from that descriptor with a strict byte cap and reject growth; add replacement/symlink/parent-race and growing-file regressions.

A fixture-only stat hook replaced an initially 2-byte allowed file with a symlink to a synthetic outside file after stat; maxBytes=4. findings.boundaryEnglish: Deterministic synthetic symlink replacement read outside-allowlist bytes. Requires local/agent write control of an allowed path; no private data was accessed.

findings.title: iOS native downloads and share backlog lack explicit byte and concurrency bounds
findings.evidence: attach() inserts every WKDownload into transfers; destination selection at lines 50-67 checks endpoint and status but not expectedContentLength/quota. downloadDidFinish() at line 82 appends to pendingShares. Cleanup at lines 24-30 is startup age-based (24 hours), not a byte budget. Same-origin redirect rejection at lines 74-76 and filename sanitization are positive controls.
findings.trigger: An allowed same-origin server supplies oversized files or the user starts many downloads while a share sheet blocks queue drainage.
findings.impact: Native temporary storage, active-transfer count and queued shares have no application-level upper bound. cancelAll() cleans active/pending entries, but a share already removed from pendingShares is retained until its completion handler; OS behavior does not supply an evidenced application quota.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit total/per-file byte limits, a small active-transfer and share backlog cap, user-visible cancellation, and deterministic partial/active-share cleanup on endpoint change. Reject oversized declared content and enforce actual bytes where supported.

findings.boundaryEnglish: Source confirms missing app-level caps; no WebKit/storage-pressure/platform tests or native build.

remediation.summary: Complete scoped source remediation and bilingual/version/security contract verified (NAT-005): Replaced the WKDownload destination writer with URLSessionDataDelegate dataTask streaming into app-owned FileHandle. Each Data chunk is counted BEFORE writing: count must fit 64 MiB minus written bytes and any known declared remainder. Overflow fails/cancels before that chunk writes; no WebKit destination, URLSession downloadTask or resume-data fallback. Two active transfers; two total active/pending/download share slots INCLUDING the active share; each admitted transfer reserves the full 64 MiB, with total reservation plus active/pending actual share bytes bounded to 128 MiB. Asynchronous cookie acquisition is already counted as an admitted transfer. Unknown declared lengths are now supported within the actual-byte prewrite bound. Oversized known lengths, non-2xx responses and nonidentity Content-Encoding fail closed. Final on-disk length must equal counted written bytes and, when known, declared length. Five-minute deadline remains; timer no longer serves as a reactive byte quota. Cancels WebKit download without supplying any destination and accepts only a same-origin original HTTP(S) GET with no body/stream. Explicit Cookie snapshot from the associated WKHTTPCookieStore is filtered by domain/path/secure/expiry/port for each request. Redirects are restricted to same scheme/host/effective port/no userinfo via Endpoint.contains, allowed HTTP redirect statuses and three hops BEFORE constructing credentials for the next hop. Ephemeral URLSession, no URLCache, Cookie or credential storage, no automatic cookie handling, explicit cache rejection, 15-second request and five-minute resource timeouts, and main-queue delegates. Ambient HTTP-auth challenges rejected; normal system server-trust validation retained. Native response cookies are not merged into WebKit. Cookie-store change clears transfers and pending/active shares, closes handles, removes staging and invalidates the session; UUID transfer ownership rejects late cookie/data/redirect callbacks while allowing fresh subsequent downloads. Endpoint/cache-clear/user cancellation/controller destruction terminally cancel the old coordinator. Existing stale-WebView checks, captured old coordinator and share-directory identity checks remain. Private UUID roots and 0700 transfer directories; file permissions 0600 with complete file protection. Failure/cancellation closes the app-owned handle before deletion. Localized EN/CN failure text states GET/blob/POST restrictions and limits.

Legacy route calls the same helper after post-upload token check; helper completion has no further original token/abort proof. Preference-only patch shifts this code but does not alter the writer contract.
Reconciliation awaits status reading then invokes patchOpenClawModels; its signature carries no request/authority or mutation-owner contract.
Writer awaits read/copy/mkdir/writeFile before rename at 38, without token/abort/owner authority checks at any filesystem effect.
ConnectorReadHandle is explicitly a delivery proof, not authorization for a mutation/native call/later transaction.

findings.trigger: A valid non-dry-run reconciliation needs to add configured aliases, then the original token is revoked or request is aborted while status/config read or another pre-commit filesystem await is pending.
findings.impact: The helper can continue backup/config replacement after authority loss; the worker's final response denial cannot undo a committed write. Missing continuity is source-confirmed; race timing was not reproduced and no real configuration was touched.
findings.recommendation: Bind non-dry-run reconciliation to an original write-authority/mutation-owner contract across pre-effect waits and the commit boundary; handle admitted/unknown outcomes without rollback fiction or replay. A post-effect read-delivery check alone is insufficient. Coordinate with the existing EXE-COMPLETE-003 filesystem binding/permission repair rather than duplicating an unsafe writer.
